PARITY-DESIGN CONSTRAINT from the operator's per-pass model requirement (recorded in full on S8 / eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a).

This story's Approach says v1 = direct Anthropic, v2 = Bedrock, "same model family and decoding params". VERIFIED against landed code: that pairing is currently UNDER-SPECIFIED in a way that can silently invalidate the report.

The gate does not run on one model. Plan-review Pass-1 runs the YAML model_ladder (plan-review.yaml:62-65: claude-haiku-4-5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6 -> claude-opus-4-8) while Pass-2/Pass-4 run the downgraded verifier model (VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = claude-sonnet-4-6 via review_kernel.resolve_verifier_model). Code review, separately, runs ALL passes on cfg.model (code-review.yaml declares no per-step model at all). So the Anthropic baseline is a MULTI-model configuration whose per-pass mapping differs between the two gates.

If v2 is a single Bedrock model id — which is all this epic's cutover knob (REBAR_LLM_MODEL) can express today — then the paired run differs in TWO variables at once: provider AND per-pass model class. Any criterion it fails is then unattributable, and any criterion it PASSES is passed by a configuration production will not actually run. Criterion (a) structured-output validity is the most exposed, since the frontier/non-frontier split is exactly what changes.

So this story needs to state, as part of the protocol rather than leaving it to the runner:
- the per-pass model mapping used on BOTH sides, pass by pass, with v2's Bedrock inference-profile id paired to the v1 Anthropic model of the SAME class (opus<->opus for Pass-1, sonnet<->sonnet for Pass-2/Pass-4);
- that the recorded ParityReport carries that mapping, so a reader can tell WHICH configuration cleared the bar;
- decoding params held equal per pass — note Pass-2 pins temperature=0 and MEASURED us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 400s on temperature=0, so a mis-paired Pass-2 does not merely diverge, it errors and lands in the error-rate criterion for the wrong reason.

Sequencing note: this makes S6 dependent on whatever resolves the per-pass config seam (currently proposed on S8) — the parity run cannot pair per-pass models that the configuration cannot express. Flagging rather than editing the dependency graph, since the seam's home is still open.

PILOT PARITY RUN (N=1) — Bedrock vs direct Anthropic, provider as the ONLY variable. Operator authorized running experiments ahead of implementation.

This is NOT the ParityReport this story's AC requires (that needs the standing eval corpus at N>=3). It is a single paired sample run to find out EARLY whether the substrate is viable at all, because if rebar's structured-output path does not survive the Converse API then S8 is blocked and the corpus run would only tell us so more expensively.

PROTOCOL: the same gate operation (`rebar review-plan`) on the SAME ticket (281f-3336-c668-4979) at the SAME `--ref HEAD`, same plan text, same code tree. Only `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` differed. Account 896586841071 / us-east-1.

  v1 direct Anthropic  model=claude-sonnet-4-6
  v2 Bedrock           model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6

RESULT — decision-level agreement is EXACT:

  |                     | v1 Anthropic          | v2 Bedrock            |
  | verdict             | PASS                  | PASS                  |
  | blocking findings   | 0                     | 0                     |
  | advisory findings   | 2                     | 2                     |
  | advisory criteria   | ac-quality (P6),      | ac-quality (P6),      |
  |                     | file-impact-cov (P9)  | file-impact-cov (P9)  |
  | llm_calls           | 4                     | 4                     |
  | runner              | pydantic_ai           | pydantic_ai           |

So on this sample: zero decision-level flips, and agreement holds at the finer CRITERION level too (the same two criteria fired, not merely the same counts). Criterion (a) structured-output validity HELD — the run completed through the Converse API with no StructuredOutputError, no contract violation, and the same call count, which is the specific thing this story flags as most at risk because Converse differs in structured-output handling.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION — LATENCY. Bedrock was ~35% slower on model time for identical work: llm_ms 26531.6 vs 19689.9 (total_ms 27135.0 vs 20305.6), same 4 calls. One sample, no concurrency, so treat as a hint not a measurement — but the parity protocol should record latency per pass, because the gate runs on the critical path of every landing and a 35% model-time regression across every Pass-1 fan-out is a throughput question S8 has not costed.

CAVEATS, stated so this is not over-read:
- N=1, one ticket, one criterion mix, PASS/PASS. A paired sample where both sides agree on an easy verdict is the weakest possible evidence of agreement; the corpus run must include tickets that BLOCK, since a flip on a blocking verdict is the failure mode that matters.
- Both sides ran SONNET. This says nothing about the opus path, which is where the per-pass model requirement (see eb6e) and the temperature defect (1903-868c-b704-4a80, which BLOCKS eb6e) both live. A parity run that only exercises sonnet would miss exactly the configuration Pass-1 is meant to use.
- Caching differed in a way that is NOT a Bedrock property: v2 reported aggregate cache_write_tokens=2132 / cache_read_tokens=0, and both runs emitted spurious per-call "caching had NO effect" warnings on sub-4096-token calls. That warning is miscalibrated on BOTH providers — filed as 7a79-a920-afe7-40cf — so it must not be read as a Bedrock caching regression when the corpus run emits it.

CORRECTION / CAVEAT ON THE N=1 PILOT ABOVE — it may not have been a true provider comparison, and I should not have recorded it without checking this.

WHAT I NOW KNOW. The Pass-1 finder does NOT run on `cfg.model`. `production_batch_runner.py:87-93` sets `cfg = replace(cfg, model=req.model_ladder[0])`, where the ladder comes from the gate YAML — `workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml:62-65` = `[claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-8]` — and the code comment states the size ladder "escalates up from here". Measured on a real Anthropic review of 281f: 41 calls on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` and 1 on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`, i.e. Pass-1 escalated to opus and Pass-2/Pass-4 took the sonnet verifier downgrade. So on the Anthropic path the operator's requirement (Pass-1 opus, Pass-2/Pass-4 sonnet) already holds.

WHY THAT THREATENS THE PILOT. Those ladder entries are BARE model names, and `config.py:333-341` maps the prefix `claude` -> `anthropic`. So during a run with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, the Pass-1 batch runner replaces cfg.model with the bare `claude-haiku-4-5`, which infers provider `anthropic`. If that is what happened, the "Bedrock" arm of my pilot ran its Pass-1 finders against DIRECT ANTHROPIC and only the non-ladder calls went to Bedrock — making the comparison Anthropic-vs-Anthropic for the pass that does most of the work, and the agreement I reported nearly meaningless as provider evidence.

WHAT I CANNOT CONCLUDE EITHER WAY. I captured only `tail -40` of the Bedrock run, so the per-call model lines for its Pass-1 are not in my log. I originally read the small number of Bedrock-named warning lines as a difference in call volume between arms; that was MY TRUNCATION, not a real asymmetry, so it is not evidence of contamination either. The honest status is: UNVERIFIED, and the pilot's PASS/PASS agreement must NOT be cited as provider parity until this is settled.

WHAT THE REAL RUN MUST DO. Capture the resolved model for EVERY call in both arms (the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` rig used by `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml:83,107-119` already records per-call model) and assert that the v2 arm made ZERO calls to a non-Bedrock provider. If any bare `claude-*` ladder entry reaches a Bedrock run, that is the split-brain and it must be fixed before the corpus run, not explained afterwards.

RELATED SHARP EDGE, independently confirmed: `review_kernel/verify.py:269` returns the verifier default ONLY when `model == default_model`. Any Bedrock id is a non-default value, so the Pass-2/Pass-4 sonnet downgrade STOPS APPLYING on the Bedrock arm while it still applies on the Anthropic arm. Both arms would then differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), which makes any criterion failure unattributable and any pass unrepresentative of production. The driver must either pin both arms' per-pass models explicitly or map them per pass.

comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION RESEARCH against the landed code. FOUR findings contradict this plan as written; recording before the story is claimed.

1. "No new gate logic is written; wiring only" IS NOT TRUE. parity_report() is pure and needs no change — it takes two index-paired sequences of ItemRecord and returns ParityReport(passed, gating_failures, metrics). But it has ZERO production callers (grep of src/ finds only container_fidelity_report, prerequisite_fidelity_report and parallel_run_and_diff), it is NOT exported from rebar.llm, there is no CLI command, and there is NO serializer — so "record the ParityReport" has no existing artifact path. More importantly there is NO ItemRecord adapter: run_eval returns {prompt, epochs, gate, passed, coverage, epoch_pass, junit} — pass/fail per EPOCH, not per-item decision+label. Building that mapping is NET-NEW work and it is load-bearing, because criterion (b) "zero decision-level flips" is scored on it.

2. GOLD COVERAGE FORCES POOLING. parity.py sets MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20 and FAILS (not silently passes) below it. No single eval spec's gold_set reaches 20 — the largest is plan-review-container at 12. So the driver MUST pool gold items across specs, or explicitly lower min_gold and justify it. Also note the CI cost rail REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES=12 used by the existing live job truncates dataset[:12], which would decapitate the two largest gold sources (plan-review-finder 42 cases, plan-review-container 24) — applying that cap here would likely trip the gold-coverage failure. Run uncapped, or cap high enough to preserve gold.

3. THE CORPUS BARELY PRODUCES BLOCKING VERDICTS. Only completion-verifier.eval.yaml scores a coarse PASS/FAIL (6 fail / 5 pass cases). Every other spec is scored on FINDINGS PRESENCE, not a verdict — several say so explicitly (code-review-security: "scored on FINDINGS presence, not a FAIL/BLOCK verdict"). This matters because the pilot recorded on this ticket was PASS/PASS, and agreement on easy PASSes is the weakest possible evidence. The decision-mapping choice (expect:finding/fail -> block, expect:pass -> advisory/dropped) is where the real design judgment sits.

4. THE TWO ARMS WOULD DIFFER IN TWO VARIABLES, NOT ONE — this is the sharpest finding and it invalidates a naive run. Flipping the provider is an ENV change (REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:...), but review_kernel/verify.py:269 returns the verifier default ONLY when model == default_model. Any Bedrock id is a non-default value, so the Pass-2/Pass-4 sonnet downgrade STOPS APPLYING on the Bedrock arm while it still applies on the Anthropic arm. Separately, Pass-1 runs the YAML model_ladder (plan-review.yaml:62-65 = haiku/sonnet/opus as BARE names), and bare "claude-*" infers provider anthropic (config.py:333-341) — so a "Bedrock" run may still send its Pass-1 finders to DIRECT ANTHROPIC. Both effects mean provider is NOT the only variable, so any criterion failure is unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production. The driver must pin per-pass models on BOTH arms explicitly, and the run must assert ZERO calls to a non-Bedrock provider on the v2 arm (the REBAR_USAGE_LOG rig already records per-call model).

COST SHAPE, so the job is sized before it is funded: ~534 model calls per arm per epoch across the 21 dataset-bearing specs; at N=3 both arms that is ~3,200 calls. At concurrency 1 (eval.py runs sequentially) that is roughly 9 hours wall clock, which EXCEEDS the 6-hour GitHub-hosted job limit — so the job needs sharding per spec (matrix) or splitting. Model the job on .github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml's eval-live (workflow_dispatch/schedule gated, continue-on-error, REBAR_USAGE_LOG summarized into the job summary), which is the existing env-gated live-LLM pattern.

SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE: this story cannot produce a valid ParityReport until the per-pass model mapping is expressible, which is the same gap recorded on eb6e and blocked by 1903 (temperature override) and a574 (region). Running the corpus before that would spend the full ~3,200 calls on a comparison that cannot be attributed.

NOTE: I myself asserted the opposite earlier in this session and had to retract it — I had confirmed the function BODY still contains the expression and wrongly inferred the rule was live. Existence is not reachability.
* It cited `plan-review.yaml`'s ladder as BARE `claude-*` names, so a "Bedrock" run would still send Pass-1 to DIRECT ANTHROPIC. Also fixed: `:62-65` now reads `[trivial, standard, frontier]` (7761), and 3768 has just declared a class on every code-review LLM step (`base`/`round_a`/`round_b` -> frontier, `verify`/`coach` -> standard), so no pass inherits a single scalar any more.
Its REMEDY, however, still stands and is now ACHIEVABLE rather than aspirational: "the driver must pin per-pass models on BOTH arms explicitly". That is exactly what the class config now expresses.

1. **Bedrock REFUSES the plain model id on-demand.** `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` fails with ValidationException: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported. comments.body:
PLAN-REVIEW GATE CLEARED — signed PASS, zero blocking findings, NO plan edit was needed.

`rebar review-plan 0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac` at REBAR_GATE_REF=HEAD returned verdict PASS with an
empty `blocking` array, and signed the attestation. `rebar review-plan 0d76 --status` now reports
`{"ok": true, "verdict": "certified", "verified_at_sha": "144bb02251ec052d71fff029b8fce71c4d12cce0"}`.
The ticket is claimable.

WHY THE DESCRIPTION WAS NOT EDITED. The plan passed as written on the first review of this round, so
every remaining finding is ADVISORY (advisory criteria never block a claim). Editing the description
now would be a material edit that invalidates the freshly signed attestation and force another
~7-minute LLM review with no guarantee of a second PASS — a strictly worse trade than carrying the
advisories into implementation. They are recorded here instead, and should be applied by whoever
claims the ticket, at implementation time.

THE FIVE ADVISORIES, in priority order:

1. [G1G2, critical-severity/advisory] The Approach understates the `parity_report` reference set. It
   names only the definition plus `container_fidelity_report` and `prerequisite_fidelity_report`;
   two more callers exist — `parity.parallel_run_and_diff` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:302`) and
   `fidelity_spot_eval` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:194`, calling
   `parity.parity_report(v1, v2, min_gold=SPOT_MIN_GOLD)`). VERIFIED at HEAD — both are real. The
   plan's load-bearing CONCLUSION is unaffected: neither is a production gate caller, so "zero
   production callers" still holds; only the enumeration is short.

2. [T8, major] Errored `ItemRecord`s can register as decision flips. `parity_report` computes
   `decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)`
   (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:106`) with NO `errored` guard, and `_DECISIONS` includes `"dropped"`
   (`parity.py:32`), so the precedent's errored-item `decision="dropped"`
   (`fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`) paired against a `block`/`advisory` v1 record counts as a flip. One
   transient throttle on a v2 gold item would then fail the slot as a Bedrock non-inferiority
   failure instead of marking it INVALID — contradicting the plan's own error-classification
   invariant. FIX AT IMPLEMENTATION: filter errored items out of the paired lists fed to
   `parity_report` (keeping them only in the classifier's own error-count fields), or exclude
   `errored` from the flip computation.

3. [T8, major] The error classifier's discrimination rule is under-specified. A temperature
   rejection is ITSELF a `ValidationException`, so "sampling-parameter rejection" and
   "validation refusal" overlap and need an explicit precedence. Also, the precedent being copied
   (`fidelity_spot_eval._record`, `:170`) uses a bare `except Exception:` that DISCARDS the
   exception — so the classifier as-shaped cannot see the string it must key on. FIX: capture each
   epoch's exception text, and classify by an ordered predicate — (1) message contains
   `temperature` -> sampling-parameter bucket; (2) `AccessDeniedException`/`ValidationException` ->
   auth/validation bucket; (3) otherwise generic errored.

4. [T3, major] The provider-clean tally technique names the wrong log format. The plan says to
   extract per-call model from lines "carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`", but
   `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is JSONL — `usage_log.py:315` writes `json.dumps(row) + "\n"` with JSON keys
   `model` / `input_tokens` (`_FIELDS`, `:32`), and `prompt-eval.yml` consumes it with
   `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize`. A `model=` grep matches nothing, defeating the
   v2-arm-provider-clean proof as written. FIX: parse each row as JSON, keep rows carrying both a
   `model` field and a non-null `input_tokens`, and tally by `model` — or reuse
   `rebar.llm.usage_log`'s own reader.

# S6 — Clear the parity bar for Bedrock before it becomes a first-class provider

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py` defines rebar's non-inferiority bar — structured-output validity, per-criterion
verdict agreement with zero decision-level flips on the gold set, recall and false-accept within 2pp, runtime
error rate, and a gold-coverage floor. It was required before the last LLM substrate swap (LangGraph →
pydantic-ai). Routing gate traffic through Bedrock is a substrate change of the same kind: a different API
surface (Converse), different capability flags, and a different structured-output path. S8 (eb6e) cuts the
production review bot over to Bedrock; without a measured bar, that cutover and the epic's "first-class
provider" tier label are unearned assertions. This story produces the measurement S8 consumes.

## Approach

Add an opt-in, operator-run provider-parity harness modeled directly on the landed spot-eval precedent
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` — same parity bar, same epoch-majority aggregation, same
committed-results-plus-offline-recheck shape. That precedent is the positive reason for the choice: it is the
one pattern in this repo that has already run a paired, live, billable two-arm comparison through
`parity.parity_report` and left reviewable evidence behind
(`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/fidelity_spot_eval_results.json`, re-scored offline by
`tests/unit/test_fidelity_spot_eval.py::test_recorded_live_results_are_within_tolerance`). Copying a proven
harness shape is cheaper and lower-risk than inventing a second one.

**Correcting an earlier claim in this plan.** A previous draft said "no new gate logic is written; wiring only".
That is FALSE and nothing here relies on it. `parity_report` itself is pure and needs no change, but it has ZERO
production callers — under `src/` the only references are its own definition and two internal reuses,
`container_fidelity_report` and `prerequisite_fidelity_report` — and `run_eval` returns
`{prompt, epochs, gate, passed, coverage, epoch_pass, junit}`, i.e. per-EPOCH pass/fail, not per-item
decision + gold label (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:622-649`). The corpus→`ItemRecord` adapter, the repeat
aggregation, the two-arm driver, the CLI and the results serializer are all NET-NEW and load-bearing, because
criterion (b) "zero decision-level flips" is scored entirely on that mapping.

### Step 1 — the probe, before any corpus spend

The assumption most likely to sink the run is that the Bedrock inference-profile ids are invokable at all in
THIS project's AWS account. Ticket 2932's operator correction records that every earlier Bedrock measurement was
taken in a different account and region and assigns the re-measurement to this story;
`infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:26-28` records a real `AccessDeniedException` on `bedrock:InvokeModel`, and a plain
on-demand id was refused with `ValidationException`. So step 1 is a probe, not the corpus: for EACH candidate
inference-profile id, one ~8-token `aws bedrock-runtime converse` call in account 896586841071 / us-east-1 — the
account of the terraform backend bucket `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` (`infra/terraform/versions.tf:14`) and the
`aws_region` default `us-east-1` (`infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5`). Each id is probed TWICE: once with no
sampling parameters, and once with `temperature=0`, the value the verifier path sends.

The probe is PER SLOT and its outcome is per slot — the two class slots ride independent profile ids, so
"invokable" is not all-or-nothing:

- Both slots invokable → run both slots.
- Only one slot invokable → run that slot, record the other slot's EXACT refusal string as its finding, and
  record `frontier_measured: false` (or `standard_measured: false`) in the results file. A one-slot run is
  explicitly NOT a pass for the unmeasured slot; the unmeasured slot becomes an open question the epic's
  first-class claim must settle before S8.
- Neither slot invokable → no corpus spend at all; the refusals are the entire deliverable.

Worked example of the partial case: if `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` returns a normal completion but
`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` returns
`ValidationException: Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported`, then the run
proceeds with the `standard` slot only; `provider_parity_results.json` contains a `standard` block with a real
`ParityReport` and a `frontier` block of
`{"measured": false, "refusal": "<the exact error string>"}`; and the ticket comment states that Bedrock cleared
the bar at `standard` and is UNMEASURED at `frontier`.

If a `temperature=0` probe 400s where the bare probe succeeded, that id must carry
`supports_temperature: False` in `capabilities._MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` before the corpus run. Both
current opus candidates are ALREADY enrolled — `capabilities.py:126-129` lists `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`
and `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (and their `global.` forms) with `supports_temperature: False`, and
`runner.py:421-427` withdraws the parameter from the request on that basis — so the probe is expected to confirm
an existing mechanism rather than discover new work. It is still run, because an id NOT on that list would 400
on every temperature-bearing case and silently convert a configuration defect into a validity / error-rate
parity failure.

### Exactly one variable between the arms

Both arms run the SAME cases through the SAME `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.run_case` path; only the model string
differs. The mechanism is `rebar.llm.config.gate_config(cfg)` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:93-101`): inside that
scope `resolve_gate_config` returns the arm's config. This is load-bearing rather than incidental, because
`runner._effective_config` substitutes `req.config.model` OVER the runner's own base config
(`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:182,209-212`) — passing a differently-configured runner alone would NOT flip the model.
Wrapping each arm in `gate_config` makes the request config and the runner agree, so provider is the only
variable and any criterion failure is attributable.

That mechanism reaches only the arms of `run_case` that resolve through `resolve_gate_config` — the plan-review
criterion arm, the novelty arm and the code-review arm
(`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:103,155,229`). It does NOT reach the three agentic disposable-store arms:
`completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality` and `spec-alignment` are dispatched to ops that resolve
`config or LLMConfig.from_env(...)` directly — `operations.py:136`, `completion.py:331`, `spec_scan.py:68` — and
`run_case` passes them no `config=`, so `gate_config` does not apply and both arms would read the same ambient
model. **Those three specs are therefore excluded from the corpus**, so the provider split cannot silently
collapse on any corpus item. (That divergence contradicts `resolve_gate_config`'s own documented invariant that
"the ops call THIS, never `from_env` directly"; it is an existing defect in those three ops, out of scope here,
and this story routes around it rather than fixing it.)

The gate's per-pass model ladder is likewise not in play: `RunRequest` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:70-118`) carries
no model-class field, so a single-prompt eval case resolves `cfg.model` and nothing else. That is why this
harness — rather than a paired `rebar review-plan` run — is the right instrument: the split-brain risk recorded
earlier on this ticket (a bare `claude-*` ladder rung silently routing a "Bedrock" arm to direct Anthropic)
cannot arise on this path.

### Arms and pairing

Same underlying model on both sides of each pair, named by class slot:

- `standard`: v1 `claude-sonnet-4-6` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:73`) ↔ v2
  `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:38`).
- `frontier`: v1 `claude-opus-4-8` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:67`) ↔ v2
  `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, subject to step 1 confirming it invokable.

Both slots are attempted because production uses both — frontier is the Pass-1 finder, standard is Pass-2 verify
and Pass-4 coach. Certifying only sonnet would leave the frontier path, which does most of the gate's work,
unmeasured, which is why an unmeasurable frontier slot is recorded as unmeasured rather than skipped silently.

### Corpus and the gold floor

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:88` sets `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20` and `parity_report` FAILS below it; no single eval spec's
gold set reaches 20 (largest: `plan-review-container.eval.yaml`, 12). So the corpus POOLS gold-labelled dataset
cases across specs. A case is eligible when its `expect` is in `{finding, fail, pass}` AND its solver id — the
case's own `criterion` field when it has one, else the spec's prompt id — resolves to a non-agentic
`run_case` arm. That yields a pool of 142 eligible cases across 15 specs. `finding` and `fail` map to the parity
decision `block`, `pass` maps to `advisory` — the same two-bucket mapping
`fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` already uses.

The run takes a deterministic stratified sample: the first `finding`/`fail` case and the first `pass` case per
spec, ordered by spec id then case id — **30 items, 15 gold-block and 15 gold-advisory** — with a recorded
corpus digest in the shape of `fidelity_spot_eval.prerequisite_corpus_digest`. 30 clears the floor of 20, so
**`min_gold` is NOT lowered**: `parity_report` is called with its default. The CI cost rail
`REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES` is deliberately not used: it truncates `dataset[:12]` per spec
(`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:654-655`) and would decapitate the largest gold sources.

Worked example of one corpus item, so the adapter's contract is unambiguous: dataset case
`G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries `expect: finding` and `criterion: G3`, so
it dispatches to the `G3` criterion arm and its gold `label` is `"block"`. Its three v2 epochs return
findings / findings / no-findings, so `_verdict_decision` yields `block, block, advisory`, the majority is
`block`, and the arm's record is `ItemRecord(valid=True, decision="block", label="block")` — a recall hit, not a
flip. Had the v1 arm's majority been `advisory` on the same item, `parity_report` would emit
`1 decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)` and `passed=False`.

### Repeats

`parity.ItemRecord`'s "averaged over the N repeats" is prose, not behaviour: `parallel_run_and_diff`
(`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:286-302`) runs each item exactly once per runner with no repeat loop and no averaging.
So this harness does NOT use `parallel_run_and_diff`. It runs its own N=3 epoch loop per case per arm and reduces
to a majority decision (ties broken toward the cautious `block`), exactly as
`fidelity_spot_eval.relocation_spot_eval(epochs=…)` and `_majority_decision` already do, then feeds the averaged
paired `ItemRecord` lists straight to `parity_report`.

### Error classification

An epoch that raises is recorded as an errored `ItemRecord` and the comparison completes rather than aborting —
but the serializer classifies the cause, so a configuration defect is never recorded as a parity verdict. A
sampling-parameter rejection (a 400 naming `temperature`) and an authorization / validation refusal are counted
and reported in their own fields, distinct from `decision_flips`. Any non-zero count of either makes the run
INVALID for that slot rather than a Bedrock failure: it is fixed and re-run, not written up as non-inferiority
evidence.

### Budget

At the both-slots ceiling: 30 cases × 2 arms × 3 epochs × 2 class slots = 360 case-runs, and every eligible arm
is single-prompt (the agentic multi-call arms are excluded above), so at most 360 model calls — halved when only
one slot is invokable, zero when neither is. Actual per-call model usage is still
measured rather than assumed, via `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` — the rig `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml:83,110-112`
already uses — and summarized into the recorded report.

### Not a GitHub Actions job

The harness is an operator-run module CLI, like `fidelity_spot_eval.main()`, which no workflow invokes. A CI job
was the earlier plan and is rejected on grounded terms: the Bedrock grant in `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:57-72`
is attached to the Gerrit **instance** role, and the only GitHub-OIDC role, `rebar-terraform-plan`
(`infra/terraform/iam.tf:166-178`, assumed at `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:34-39`), is
`ReadOnlyAccess` — so a CI arm would first require a new Bedrock-capable OIDC role, which is unfunded work
outside this story. Auth is therefore the ambient AWS credential chain
(`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:10,55-88`) with `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1` set explicitly
(`src/rebar/llm/config.py:569-571`), plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the v1 arm. Region is set explicitly because an
unresolvable region otherwise surfaces as a bare boto3 `NoRegionError` from deep inside client construction
(`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:67-87`).

### Decision-bearing

If Bedrock fails any criterion, or a slot cannot be measured, this ticket records that outcome and the epic's
first-class claim for Bedrock is revisited before the S8 cutover proceeds, rather than shipping a tier label the
evidence does not support.

### Out of scope — cited, not absorbed

The sub-4096-token "caching had NO effect" warning is miscalibrated on BOTH providers (bug
7a79-a920-afe7-40cf); it must not be read as a Bedrock caching regression when this run emits it.
`MODEL_LADDER`'s equal sonnet/opus context limits (1157) and the mis-located escalation START rung for a
non-Anthropic-family primary (48b3) affect ladder escalation, which this harness does not exercise.
`infer_provider`'s `gemini` → `google_genai` mapping (5267) is unrelated to the `bedrock:` prefix. The three
agentic ops' bypass of `resolve_gate_config` is worked around by corpus exclusion, not fixed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py` (new) — the corpus selector and digest, the two-arm `gate_config`
  driver, the epoch-majority `ItemRecord` adapter, the `parity_report` call, the error classifier, the results
  serializer, and the `main()` CLI including the per-slot step-1 invokability and temperature probes.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` (new) — the committed recorded run: per class slot
  either a `ParityReport` block or a `{"measured": false, "refusal": …}` block, plus each arm's resolved model
  id, the corpus digest, the epoch count, the error-classification counts and the per-arm call/latency summary.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` (new) — the offline tests below, using `FakeRunner`.
- This ticket's comments — the quoted probe outcomes and `ParityReport` verdict.

## Testing

Offline, in `make test`, no model and no credentials:

- Happy path: two agreeing arms over a fixture corpus produce `passed=True` with zero decision flips.
- Failure path: a candidate arm that flips one gold decision produces `passed=False` and the emitted
  `gating_failures` names `decision-level flip(s) on the gold set`.
- Edge: a corpus below the gold floor fails on the coverage guard alone, mirroring
  `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py::test_goldless_run_fails_coverage_guard`.
- Edge: an arm whose runner raises records an `errored` `ItemRecord` and the comparison completes rather than
  aborting.
- Edge: a raised 400 naming `temperature` is counted as a sampling-parameter rejection and marks the slot
  INVALID, not as a decision flip.
- Edge: the corpus selector excludes every case dispatching to `completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality` or
  `spec-alignment`, and returns at least 20 gold items from the remaining specs.
- Recheck: the committed `provider_parity_results.json` is re-scored against the same parity bar with no model
  call, mirroring `test_recorded_live_results_are_within_tolerance`.

Live, opt-in, operator-run, never in default CI:

- Step 1, the per-slot probe: each candidate inference-profile id is invoked once bare and once with
  `temperature=0`, and both outcomes recorded, before any corpus spend.
- Step 2: the paired corpus run at N=3 per arm for each invokable slot, with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` used to assert
  the v2 arm made ZERO calls resolving to a non-Bedrock provider. Extract per-call model only from log lines
  carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`; a whole-log grep for the model id over-counts, because
  verdict-JSON fields match the same string.

- [x] [operator-attested] Step 1's per-slot probe result for account 896586841071 / us-east-1 is recorded as a
